title.narrative: Developing and Promoting Peacebuilding in Kachin and northern Shan

description.narrative: Contract related to: Developing and Promoting Peacebuilding in Kachin and northern Shan - the Overall Objective of the action is to contribute to lasting peace, security, stability and sustainable development while promoting human rights, democracy and gender equality in Myanmar. The Specific Objective of the action is to contribute towards building resilience and peace with and through local actors. The expected outputs are the following:1.      The humanitarian-development-peace nexus in Myanmar addressing immediate needs, human rights,  reduce vulnerabilities, and increase resilience is reinforced;2.      Capacities, confidence and trust among local peace actors and communities allowing for an inclusive political dialogue and peace-making process are strengthened; 3.      Capacity and autonomy of local Civil Society Organisations to deliver services, and promote and protect civil rights in Myanmar are enhanced.The action responds to the urgent requirement to focus on reducing vulnerabilities and increasing resilience of conflict affected populations by addressing immediate needs and human rights, through the provision of basic services, livelihood opportunities, the protection of human rights and a medium/long term goal of creating a space for a possible peaceful resolution of the crisis. The action aims at women¿s meaningful participation in future political dialogue, peace negotiations, and peace-building and reconciliation efforts. Furthermore, the action is grounded in two concepts: a focus on flexibility, in joining humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding approaches, and a focus on civil society and localized response led by trusted community-based organizations, as both a transformative approach and as a mechanism of true sustainability and accountability.The action corresponds to the priority of supporting peace and durable solutions, in line with the programming exercise carried out until January 2021. This priority remains valid also under the changed circumstances, however, the means and ways of implementation require to be adjusted to bring them in line with the increasing basic needs of larger segments of the society and the focus on working with and through civil society actors. It is also in line with strategic discussions with Member States to provide a coordinated response during the coming two years and in the absence of a MIP. The action will be implemented in coordination and complementarity with the EU Instrument contributing to Stability and Peace IcSP and the NDICI crisis response interventions. This action contributes primarily to SDG 16 ¿Promote just, peaceful and inclusive societies¿. It also contributes to SDG 10 ¿Reduced inequalities¿ as well as SDG 1 aimed at ending poverty and SDG 5 on gender equality.

title.narrative: SO 2: to support and build selfreliant communities and address emerging immediate needs

description.narrative: Community and individual resilience is integrated across and strongly linked to peace as resources and capacity are needed to get through and emerge stronger out of the dire current situation. A stronger, more resilient community stands a better chance of building a more peaceful society in the present and in the future. Being selfreliant also means having the flexibility to adapt as per the situation and would enable/ allow communities to utilize the resources and capacity to recover from the crises, either immediate or protracted. Looking it from the other side and put more boldly, when there is no food to eat; when there is no job and food security individual, family and community level peace cannot be achieved. This need is urgent, as people in Kachin and northern Shan perceive their financial situation to be more difficult now than three years ago, and this Actions target group is less optimistic about future opportunities and their economic selfreliance . Not having proper rule of law is leading to more criminal activity and robbery affecting society and families. When the authorities are not trustworthy and in fact have become a threat and when the community needs to take care of their own security and wellbeing, it becomes even harder to consider what peace means. Due to the pandemic and political crisis and continuous armed conflict, conflictaffected populations across the state have increased, with severe threats to their resilience and ability to be selfreliant. It has also meant more complex forms of return and resettlement need supporting, with or without the engagement of authorities especially as an increased part of the target group indicates that they feel worried and not prepared for return and resettlement . The threat of conflict has increased the need to prepare for future emergencies. Indeed, emergency needs, including basic food supply, have increased significantly. unemployment, especially in KCA, the increase of food prices, land grabbing, lack of financial access, and inflation are all putting pressure on peoples livelihoods

A stronger, more resilient community stands a better chance of building a more peaceful society in the present and in the future. Being selfreliant also means having the flexibility to adapt as per the situation and would enable/ allow communities to utilize the resources and capacity to recover from the crises, either immediate or protracted. Looking it from the other side and put more boldly, when there is no food to eat; when there is no job and food security individual, family and community level peace cannot be achieved. This need is urgent, as people in Kachin and northern Shan perceive their financial situation to be more difficult now than three years ago, and this Actions target group is less optimistic about future opportunities and their economic selfreliance . Not having proper rule of law is leading to more criminal activity and robbery affecting society and families. When the authorities are not trustworthy and in fact have become a threat and when the community needs to take care of their own security and wellbeing, it becomes even harder to consider what peace means. Due to the pandemic and political crisis and continuous armed conflict, conflictaffected populations across the state have increased, with severe threats to their resilience and ability to be selfreliant. It has also meant more complex forms of return and resettlement need supporting, with or without the engagement of authorities especially as an increased part of the target group indicates that they feel worried and not prepared for return and resettlement . The threat of conflict has increased the need to prepare for future emergencies. Indeed, emergency needs, including basic food supply, have increased significantly. unemployment, especially in KCA, the increase of food prices, land grabbing, lack of financial access, and inflation are all putting pressure on peoples livelihoods

title.narrative: SO 4: To empower local communities and strengthen civil society organisations

description.narrative: Despite increased restrictions to humanitarian access, including targeted arrests and movement blocks, local humanitarian actors and CSOs are responding with community assistance, even risking their own safety and security. title.narrative: SO 01: To promote local peacebuilding and social cohesion among and within communities

description.narrative: Since the coup in Myanmar, the formal peace process has been in a dead lock on every level and the commitment of key actors has come to a stop. This has increased the need for strengthening of, and finding new opportunities for, local peace building processes. Through this specific objective existing local peace building mechanisms will be strengthened, and new mechanisms will be explored both are urgently needed and critical for a peaceful community. Due to current political developments, there are many emerging peace building related issues that need to be addressed, however the existing key local actors (the Peace Talk Creation Group and the Kachin National Consultative Assembly, amongst others) are absent. In this context there is a need to create safe, conducive and productive dialogue spaces amongst different youth, women, cultural and civil society groups with a clear objective to build and maintain trust between and within communities. Engagement and advocacy with the decisionmakers will continue, where possible and without putting at risk the consortium or target group. It is important to address strengthening and building the communitybased conflict resolution mechanisms in the current political dynamics. Conflict resolution related capacity needs, including on conflict mediation, analysis, and dialogue facilitation, to be provided to local communities to play leading roles in local peacerelated process and contribute to a strengthened social cohesion. Mental health across the target area has been deteriorating and if this is not addressed in a timely and effective manner, potential future tension will build. As the current information provision has been compromised, communities must have up to date awareness on conflict drivers and the political arena to build common understanding among the communities.

title.narrative: SO 3: To strengthen womens rights and capacity for leading and participating in the economic, societal and political decisionmaking for sustainable peace building

description.narrative: The multiple ongoing crises have had a severe effect on women. Womens reproductive burden has increased significantly following the COVID19 pandemic and the military coup. Women have taken on multiple roles such as caring work, home schooling to children, and economic activities for their family. The heavy workload burden of women must be recognized and supported, and this Action seeks to contribute to a reduction of these burdens. As has been resoundingly reiterated by women peacebuilders and in WROs activism efforts, womens meaningful participation in peace and security is vital to achieving genderjust and sustainable peace in Myanmar. In the current situation, although peace in this case is referred to on an interpersonal, household and community level rather than state and national level, this Action does envision to network with other projects and encourage women peacebuilders to get involve in regional and state level networks. By including such collective action, the consortium will support more longerterm change. There is a need to revisit promoting basic gender concepts, addressing existing gender, social and traditional norms for attitude and behaviour change of male and female community members. Creating women only spaces in targeted communities and enhance womens experiences is critical to support women empowerment journey. Capacity building and skill strengthening support to enhance their power within, mobilize community to challenge and address existing norms and practices, creating spaces for women, addressing existing SGBV in community and support community to create safe environment for women, address unequal power relation between men and women, encourage women to get participate and influence in decision making body at different levels. Men will be targeted to be included in activities under this specific objective to ensure more sustainable impact.
